gloss: words of praise; laudatory title; honorific appellation

definitions.gloss: words of praise; laudatory title; honorific appellation
definitions.explanation: A formal word or phrase used to praise or honor someone or something. Can refer to honorary titles, laudatory epithets, or expressions of commendation. Used in literary, ceremonial, and formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {王|おう}に{称辞|しょうじ}が{贈|おく}られた。
examples.english: A laudatory title was bestowed upon the king.

examples.japanese: {受賞者|じゅしょうしゃ}に{対|たい}して{称辞|しょうじ}を{述|の}べた。
examples.english: Words of praise were spoken for the award recipient.

examples.japanese: 「{日本|にほん}のエジソン」という{称辞|しょうじ}で{知|し}られるその{発明家|はつめいか}は、{生涯|しょうがい}で{百以上|ひゃくいじょう}の{特許|とっきょ}を{取得|しゅとく}した。
examples.english: The inventor known by the laudatory title "the Edison of Japan" obtained over a hundred patents in his lifetime.

notes:
Composed of {称|しょう} (praise, title) and {辞|じ} (words, speech). A literary and formal term for expressions of praise or honorary designations. Often encountered in historical texts, ceremonial speeches, and formal writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {称辞|しょうじ}を{贈|おく}る: to bestow a laudatory title
- {称辞|しょうじ}を{述|の}べる: to deliver words of praise
- {最高|さいこう}の{称辞|しょうじ}: the highest praise

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {賛辞|さんじ}: praise, compliment — more commonly used in modern Japanese
- {称号|しょうごう}: title, designation — focuses on the title itself rather than the words of praise
- {敬称|けいしょう}: honorific title — specifically refers to polite forms of address (さん, 様, etc.)
